title: 11. I Did It
reviewMethod: English read-aloud translation compared with every original Korean page

pages.text: During free play in the Rainbow Class, Toto tied a red scarf around their neck and jumped up. I'm the hero, Toto Man! A hero protects friends! Whoosh, whoosh! Toto flew bravely around the classroom.
Toto Man grew more and more excited, dashing between chairs and past the block tower. Out of my way, villains! The friends worried. Toto, be careful! You'll bump into something! But Toto kept going.
Then Toto's arm knocked Hori's red toy car. Thump! It fell to the floor, rolled over, and a wheel snapped off. My car! Tears filled Hori's eyes.
Teacher Sheep came over. Who did this? Toto's heart sank. Hiding both hands behind their back, Toto blurted out, It wasn't me! I didn't do it! A lie had slipped out.
Then Kongi said, But I saw Toto do it. Toto's face grew hot. Feeling embarrassed and angry, Toto pushed Kongi, who landed with a thump. Ouch! The classroom fell silent.
The friends slowly moved away, leaving Toto alone. Toto looked at a reflection in the window. With that cape on, Toto looked less like a hero and more like a bad villain from a cartoon.
Toto's heart ached. A hero is supposed to protect friends, but I made mine cry. I broke the car, told a lie, and pushed Kongi. A tear fell. Today I really acted like a villain.
Toto found the courage to stand before the friends. Those legs trembled, but Toto stayed there. In a small, clear voice, Toto said, I did it. I broke the car and pushed Kongi. I'm sorry I lied.

Toto took Kongi's hand and helped them up. Kongi, did it hurt? I'm really sorry. Then Toto and Hori used tape to repair the toy car. A hero protects friends. From now on, I really will. The friends smiled.

They all played happily together again. Now Toto knew that saying, I did it, honestly after a mistake was real courage. Instead of being a hero, I just want to be a good friend! Hori's tail sparkled like a rainbow, and everyone laughed.
